chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever affliction befalls you, it is on account of what your hands have wrought.'

'What is your view of what hit Ali and the People of his Household (peace be upon them) after him? Is it due to what their hands had wrought, and they are the Pure People of the Household, the Infallible?'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to turn to Allah and seek His Forgiveness during every day and night, one hundred times, without having sinned. Indeed, Allah Particularizes His Guardians with afflictions in order to recompense them for them without having sinned.'
ai.seo_question: Why do the Infallible Imams suffer if they are free from sin?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi resolves the apparent contradiction between Quran 42:30, which links calamities to human deeds, and the doctrine of Ismah (infallibility) of the Ahl al-Bayt. Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that their sufferings are not punitive but are a special divine favor (fadl) intended to multiply their reward, paralleling the Prophet Muhammad’s practice of seeking forgiveness (istighfar) without sin. This establishes that afflictions for the Infallibles serve as a means of spiritual elevation rather than expiation of guilt.
